newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Netanyahu, Arafat set Thursday meeting on peace.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat set Thursday meeting on peace.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday he had "very productive" talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and they would meet again on the Israel-Gaza border on Thursday.

Netanyahu, standing next to Arafat, was speaking after they had held a some 40-minute meeting at the World Economic Forum. Arafat confirmed that the Thursday meeting, in the town of Erez, would take place.
"Chairman Arafat and I have just had a very productive meeting," said Netanyahu.

"We are going to meet again in Erez on Thursday in order to discuss specific implementation steps by both Israel and the Palestinians on the agreement that we have reached following Hebron," he added.

"We begin the various negotiations that we have discussed the following week as well, and we view this meeting in Davos as an opportunity to effectively chart the course, the practical course, for the post-Hebron negotiations and implementation."

Arafat, who was earlier reported by Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak as "pessimistic" on the situation after last month's accord on Israeli withdrawal from most of the West Bank town, said the Erez meeting would be "to discuss all these matters which have not been implemented".
